tweets.text:
One thing I’ve found interesting about exchange liquidity.

Volume doesn’t tell the whole story.

An exchange can have high volume without having great liquidity when you actually trade.

What matters is order book depth, active liquidity, and how much your order moves the price.

Trading costs are a good way to see this in practice.

For a $10K market order, we’re looking at the base tier taker fee plus half the effective spread.

That cost varies quite a bit across major venues. On perps, the gap is even bigger.

I also noticed on DeFiLlama that MEXC is now ranking #2 in active liquidity among all tracked exchanges, with $3.436B, behind only Binance at $4.065B.

A $10K trade on MEXC costs roughly half as much as on Binance or Bybit, for both spot and perps.

So volume is only one piece of the picture.

The more interesting question is how much usable liquidity is actually there when you need to trade, and what it costs to access it.
